chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sold the service of the Mudabbir (a slave manumitted upon the master's death) but did not sell his neck (full ownership). The way to reconcile between these narrations and the narrations that included the sale of the Mudabbir in all cases is that we say: If the master wishes to sell the neck (full ownership) of the slave, he needs to annul his Tadbir (manumission upon death), just as when he makes a will and then wishes to change it, he needs to annul his will, because it is in the position of a will. So if he annuls the Tadbir, it is permissible for him to sell the Mudabbir in all cases. And if he does not wish to annul his Tadbir and prefers to leave it in its state, it is permissible for him to sell its service for the duration of its life and stipulate with the buyer. And when the one who was Tadbir-ed dies, he becomes free. And that which indicates this distinction is...

key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرِ: the Mudabbir (slave manumitted upon master's death)

ai.seo_question: Can a master sell a Mudabbir slave's service or full ownership, and how is the Tadbir annulled?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the legal mechanism for selling a *Mudabbir* by distinguishing between selling their service while maintaining the manumission contract, or selling their full ownership by revoking the *Tadbir*. This distinction resolves apparent contradictions in earlier reports by establishing that the master's intent determines whether the slave remains bound to the deferred manumission or becomes fully transferable property.
